record.original_question: What is the deeper conceptual reason that Schrödinger operators with complex-valued potentials can violate locality, or equivalently the Weyl-type locality behavior that underlies the usual hbar^{-d} semiclassical scale?

evidence.quote: Abstract. We explain in which sense Schrödinger operators with complex potentials appear to violate locality (or Weyl's asymptotics), and we pose three open problems related to this phenomenon.
An even vaguer question is to understand from a more conceptual point of view the deeper reason behind a potential violation of locality.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider Schrödinger operators of the form $H = -\hbar^2 \Delta + V$ acting on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, where $V : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{C}$ is a (sufficiently decaying) complex-valued potential. For real-valued $V$, the classical Weyl law and its semiclassical refinements yield asymptotics of eigenvalue sums (or Riesz means) of the form
$$\sum_j |\lambda_j(H)|^\gamma \;\sim\; c_{\gamma,d}\, \hbar^{-d} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} V_-(x)^{\gamma + d/2}\, dx \qquad (\hbar \to 0),$$
which is local in the sense that the contribution of two disjoint pieces of the potential adds up. By contrast, for complex-valued $V$, all currently known bounds for sums of moduli of (discrete) eigenvalues take the form
$$\sum_j |\lambda_j(H)|^\gamma \;\le\; C\left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} |V(x)|^{q}\, dx \right)^{p}$$
with $p > 1$, so that disjoint pieces of $V$ no longer contribute additively; this superadditive (non-local) behavior is incompatible with the standard $\hbar^{-d}$ Weyl-type semiclassical scaling.

Problem. Identify a precise conceptual mechanism explaining why complex-valued potentials force this loss of locality, i.e. why no Weyl-type bound that is additive over disjoint supports of $V$ can hold for the eigenvalue sums of $-\hbar^2\Delta + V$ when $V$ is complex. Formulate and prove a structural statement (for instance, a no-go theorem, an obstruction tied to pseudospectral or non-self-adjoint phenomena, or an alternative semiclassical scale replacing $\hbar^{-d}$) that accounts for the observed violation of locality and the failure of the usual Weyl asymptotics in the non-self-adjoint setting.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is explicitly posed as an open problem in a September 2024 work by Cuenin and Frank on violation of locality for Schrödinger operators with complex potentials. No subsequent publication appears to provide a conceptual explanation; related work (e.g., on sparse complex potentials and logarithmic violations of Weyl's law) confirms the phenomenon but does not resolve the underlying conceptual reason.

status_evidence.title: Open problem: Violation of locality for Schrödinger operators with complex potentials
status_evidence.snippet: We explain in which sense Schrödinger operators with complex potentials appear to violate locality (or Weyl's asymptotics), and we pose three open problems related to this phenomenon.
status_evidence.claim: The conceptual reason for the locality violation is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Violation of locality for Schrödinger operators with complex potentials (CIRM notes)
status_evidence.snippet: All known bounds have p>1, meaning disjoint pieces of the potential do not contribute additively — a loss of locality.
status_evidence.claim: The non-additive structure of bounds for complex potentials is recognized but unexplained at a conceptual level.

status_evidence.title: Schrödinger Operators with Complex Sparse Potentials
status_evidence.snippet: Logarithmic violation of Weyl's law for complex sparse potentials.
status_evidence.claim: Related work confirms the phenomenon without providing the conceptual mechanism.
